title: Canonical set-valued stalk equivalence for any algebraically closed extension
statement: Let K,Ks,Omega be fields in Type u, with Ks a separable closure of K [def-pd-separable-closure], Omega algebraically closed, compatible K- and Ks-algebra structures, and a scalar tower K->Ks->Omega. Let J be the small etale topology on Spec K [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], p the point Spec Omega->Spec K [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], G=Gal(Ks/K) with Krull topology, and w=max(u+1,v). There is an equivalence Eset:Sh(J,Type w) ≌ DiscreteContAction(Type w,G) and a natural underlying-set stalk comparison j. For every sheaf F, g in G, K-automorphism tau of Omega satisfying tau|Ks=g, etale X, pointed lifts x,x' with x'=Spec(tau) followed by x, and section z in F(X), j identifies the g-translate of the germ at x with the germ at x'. In particular Omega need not be algebraic over K; the representable-stalk comparison is not part of this statement.

proof.text: Represent an element of $F_{\bar s}$ by a triple $(U,\bar u,t)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For $\sigma\in G$, change the lift to $\bar u\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\tilde\sigma)$, where $\tilde\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega/K)$ extends $\sigma$. This is independent of the extension: each point of the etale $K$-scheme $U$ has finite separable residue field by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], so an automorphism fixing $K^{\rm sep}$ fixes every such lift. The action is functorial on triples; the stabilizer of this element contains $\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\rm sep}/L)$ for the finite separable image $L\subseteq K^{\rm sep}$ of its residue field, hence is open.

proof.text: For each etale $K$-scheme $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf] makes $h_X$ a sheaf. By [lem-galois-stalk-representable], evaluation on a pointed neighbourhood identifies its stalk with $\operatorname{Hom}_K(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,X)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], $X$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $K$; every $K$-embedding of any such extension in $\Omega$ lands in $K^{\rm sep}$. Thus restriction gives a natural bijection with $\operatorname{Hom}_K(\operatorname{Spec}K^{\rm sep},X)$, compatible with the action from step 1. This proves (ii).

proof.text: First let A be the subfield of Omega of elements algebraic over K. It is an algebraic closure of K containing Ks. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], every pointed lift to an etale K-scheme factors uniquely through Spec A. These natural bijections identify the pointed-neighbourhood diagrams, their stalks, and their germ maps. Automorphisms of Omega restrict to A, and the identifications respect the action. Apply [lem-exc-field-sections-stalk-invariants] at A, where its algebraicity hypothesis holds, and transfer its section bijections and embedding-compatibility formulas to Omega. Thus sections over each finite separable L are the invariants under its fixing subgroup. Decompose each etale K-scheme into finite separable components using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points]; its sections are the product of their sections by the sheaf condition. Equivariant stalk maps therefore give natural maps on all sections, and the invariant-section bijections show this construction is inverse to taking stalks. This proves full faithfulness.

source.place: Tag 03QT, theorem-equivalence-sheaves-point, proof, inverse and omitted full-faithfulness details; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point, direct proof

proof.text: Decompose a discrete continuous G-set M in Type w into its orbits. Each orbit is finite since its stabilizer is open in the compact absolute Galois group, and can be realized in Type u. Apply [lem-exc-etale-field-gsets] to each such small orbit, giving an etale K-scheme X for it. The representable sheaf of X exists by [lem-weil-pbc-small-etale-representable-presheaf-sheaf], and its stalk is that orbit by step 2 and [lem-galois-stalk-representable]. Form the coproduct of these representable sheaves in Type w, indexed by the orbit set in Type w. The stalk preserves coproducts; the action on germs commutes with coproduct injections, so the resulting stalk is M as a G-set. This avoids requiring the entire orbit coproduct scheme to belong to the smaller site universe. Together with step 3, essential surjectivity gives the equivalence.
